subtype: Hiding behind a parent at a party [Actor]
passage:
I'm Chaitanya, Pradeep's uncle. At his cousin's birthday party, four-year-old Pradeep spent the first hour stuck to his mother's leg, face pressed into her dupatta. When aunties bent down to say hello, he hid further. One aunty said, "Arre, say hi, don't be shy!" and he started to cry.
His mother didn't push. She sat on the floor at the edge of the room with him on her lap and watched the games. After a while he peeked. Then he pointed at the bubble machine. Soon he was chasing bubbles, checking over his shoulder that she was still there.

qa.q: What did Pradeep point at after he peeked?
qa.a: The bubble machine.

qa.q: Why did Pradeep hide further when aunties bent down to say hello?
qa.a: The noisy party and the strangers felt scary, and staying hidden against his mother gave him relief.

qa.q: Which choice of his mother's helped, and why?
qa.a: Sitting at the edge of the room with him on her lap without pushing, so he felt safe enough to peek and then join in.

qa.q: How might the aunty who said 'don't be shy' have felt when Pradeep cried?
qa.a: Probably surprised and a bit awkward, since she didn't mean to upset him and didn't see that pushing made him more scared.

grounding: An uncle watches a four-year-old cling to his mother at a party, and sees gentle closeness, not pushing, help him join in.

Friday: At the neighbour's housewarming, Asif, five, clung to Abba's leg and wouldn't look at anyone. Karthik uncle said, "Come, beta, shake hands!" Asif buried his face and whimpered. Abba picked him up.
Sunday: At the Eid lunch, Abba sat with Asif in the quiet corner by the window. Abba didn't say "go and play". He just pointed things out: "Look, a kite."
Next Saturday: At the school fair, Asif held Abba's hand, then let go to stroke the rabbit at the petting stall. He looked back. Abba nodded. Asif stayed with the rabbit for ten minutes.

qa.q: What did Karthik uncle say to Asif at the housewarming?
qa.a: "Come, beta, shake hands!"

qa.q: Why did Asif bury his face when he was asked to shake hands?
qa.a: Meeting people at a busy party felt scary, and hiding against Abba's leg felt like relief.

qa.q: Which of Abba's choices helped Asif most, and why?
qa.a: Staying close without pushing, sitting in a quiet corner and pointing things out, so Asif slowly felt safe enough to let go at the fair.

qa.q: What might Abba have felt when Asif let go of his hand at the fair?
qa.a: Proud and relieved, seeing his patience help Asif take a small brave step.

grounding: Over three gatherings a five-year-old who hides behind his father is helped by patient nearness rather than pushing.

subtype: Hiding behind a parent at a party [Actor]
passage:
The rain moved the wedding reception indoors, and the small hall was packed and loud with drums. Six-year-old Omkar pressed himself behind his father, Tushar, gripping his kurta and refusing to say namaste to anyone. A great-aunt pinched his cheek, and he burst into tears.
Tushar crouched down. "Too loud?" Omkar nodded. There was no quiet room, so Tushar carried him to the corridor by the kitchen and sat on the steps with him, away from the drums. They shared a jalebi. After a while Omkar asked, "Can we look from the door?" They watched the dancing from the doorway.

qa.q: What did Omkar and Tushar share on the steps?
qa.a: A jalebi.

qa.q: Why did Omkar grip Tushar's kurta and refuse to say namaste?
qa.a: The loud, crowded hall felt overwhelming, and hiding behind his father was a way to feel safe.

qa.q: What choice did Tushar make when there was no quiet room, and why did it work?
qa.a: He took Omkar to the corridor steps away from the drums and let him choose when to watch from the door, offering nearness instead of pushing.

qa.q: How might the great-aunt have felt when Omkar burst into tears?
qa.a: Surprised and perhaps a little hurt, since she meant the cheek-pinch kindly.

grounding: At a loud, rain-crowded wedding a six-year-old hides behind his father, who finds a quieter spot and lets him approach at his own pace.

subtype: Hiding behind a parent at a party [Actor]
passage:
The colony terrace in Hyderabad was full of fairy lights, music and people for the New Year party. Akash, four, held on to his mother Jahnavi's leg with both arms. When a neighbour uncle waved, Akash pushed his face into her salwar. "Say hello, na?" someone laughed. Akash squeezed harder.

Jahnavi didn't pull him off. She sat on a plastic chair near the edge, lifted him onto her knee and let him watch. Slowly his grip loosened. He peeped at the children blowing whistles. Then he slid down, stood beside her chair, and took a whistle from the girl next door.

qa.q: What did Akash do when a neighbour uncle waved?
qa.a: Akash pushed his face into her salwar.

qa.q: Why might hiding in his mother's salwar feel good to Akash?
qa.a: Hiding shuts out the lights, noise and faces all at once, so Akash probably feels a rush of relief. Being pressed against Jahnavi also feels safe.

qa.q: Which choice of Jahnavi's helped Akash join in, and why?
qa.a: Choosing to sit near the edge with Akash on her knee instead of pulling him off. Being close to her let him watch safely until he was ready to step out himself.

qa.q: How might the neighbour uncle feel when Akash hides, and what would change if he waited instead of waving straight away?
qa.a: The uncle may feel a little brushed off, or think Akash is being rude. If he waited and just smiled from a distance, Akash might peek out sooner, because nothing would be pushing him.

grounding: A four-year-old clings to his mother's leg and won't greet anyone at a party, and gentle closeness rather than pressure helps him join in.

passage:
The doorbell rang again. Nikita, five, ran behind Papa and grabbed his shirt.

"Nikki! Come, meet Bua's new in-laws," Dadi called.

"No," Nikita whispered into Papa's back.

"She's so shy!" Bua laughed. "Come, give a namaste!"

Gautam reached back and found her small fingers. "She'll say it later. She's my helper today. Right, Nikki?"

A nod against his back.

"How many laddoos on this plate, Nikki?"

A long pause. "...Seven."

"Can you put one in each bowl?"

She stepped out, just halfway, to drop them in. A tall man smiled at her. She ducked back, then peeped again.

qa.q: What did Nikita whisper into Papa's back?
qa.a: She whispered "No".

qa.q: What shows that Nikita still feels unsure even after she starts helping?
qa.a: She stepped out only halfway, and when the tall man smiled, she ducked back before peeping again. She is testing whether it's safe, not fully relaxed yet.

qa.q: What could Gautam try if Nikita stays hidden for the rest of the evening?
qa.a: Keep giving her small jobs beside him, like handing out bowls, and let her greet people with a wave when she's ready. Staying near without forcing a namaste keeps the relief of hiding from becoming the only way to cope.

qa.q: How might Bua feel about Gautam saying "She'll say it later"?
qa.a: Bua might feel a little embarrassed in front of the new in-laws, or think Nikita is being spoiled. But she also gets to see Nikita join in, which a forced namaste might not have given her.

grounding: A five-year-old hides behind her father when relatives arrive, and her father's gentle nearness and a small task help her come out slowly.
